extracted.intended_audience: open-source investigators (Bellingcat Justice & Accountability Unit) conducting online investigations into incidents in Ukraine for possible legal accountability
extracted.subtask_description: A standard operating procedure for investigators conducting court-focused online open-source investigations into incidents in Ukraine, designed to ensure material is gathered in a manner suitable for legal proceedings. Covers systems/resources, preparation, discovery, verification, reporting, preservation and legal/ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated device and account separation
rubrics_metrics.description: You are expected to use a dedicated work device for your Justice and Accountability investigations. It is not for personal use. Ensure the hard drive of your laptop is encrypted and that you have set a very strong password. You will need to use separate user accounts for any other Bellingcat work which is not Justice & Accountability work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the same device for personal use and investigations. If you must use same device for personal tasks, do them in a separate browser window and record reasons and notify team lead. Power off laptop when not in use or at risk of theft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and configuration of VPN
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be provided with a virtual private network. Ensure the exit node is set to the USA, due to some search engine results being restricted in Europe. If an alternate node is used, permission must be sought from the lead investigator and a memo recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn on your VPN before beginning any part of your investigation to shield your online identity. If using a non-standard VPN, lead investigator approval and a memo explaining the decision are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install and use Hunchly to record browsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Install Hunchly on Chrome. Create a case in Hunchly for the incident, name it with the incident ID and turn it on so all pages visited in that Chrome window are recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not edit your Hunchly dashboard. Use a separate browser for unrelated tasks to reduce noise. If personal data is accidentally recorded, consult the lead researcher. Turn Hunchly off and close tabs when finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of centralized cloud and named folder structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an Investigation Folder in the Ukraine-specific Google Drive named with the incident ID and include: Incident Assessment Google Doc (CIVXXXX Incident Assessment), Research Notes doc (CIVXXXX Research Notes - INVESTIGATOR NAME), CIVXXXX Links Google Sheet, Hunchly files folder, Images and Videos folder, Misc folder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no duplicate folder creation. Upload content you want saved into the Incident folder. Maintain consistent naming conventions for files and folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain specific Google Sheets and Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided Google Sheets and Docs such as Incident Seed Data (CIVHARM), Ukraine Witness Sheet, Device Log Sheet, Mnemonic Preservation Sheet, Incident Link Sheet, Research Notes and Incident Assessment docs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record device and research account details in Device Sheet. Use Research Notes to log searches and rationale so investigation is replicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and use virtual research identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Create virtual identities on all major social media platforms to protect real identity and to reduce algorithmic tailoring. Record research account information in Device Sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Facebook and Twitter research accounts are required to access information. For YouTube and Instagram, access without account is possible but ensure signed out of personal accounts. Conduct initial searches while signed in to research accounts so algorithms learn relevant content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact or interact with sources without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: You should never reach out to a source or make any kind of interaction with an account without further authorisation. If you believe that a source would be crucial to reach out to, communicate this to the lead investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests to contact sources must be escalated. Use Signal for particularly sensitive communications among team if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record searches and maintain Research Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure to record the key words you search and take note of your most successful advanced searches (both to make your investigation replicable and to ensure you can pick up where you left off). Maintain a search log in the Research Notes document; record reasons for searches and any variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record which search engines were used and explain any unusual tools or techniques. Note small variations and why they were run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language coverage for searches
rubrics_metrics.description: When you create a new research account, you will need to conduct investigation-related searches in English, Ukrainian and Russian while signed in so that the algorithms learn the content you are interested in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for algorithms to adapt; ensure searches are performed in the relevant languages for comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of information: Examinable vs Descriptive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate sources: (i) Examinable/core content — granular online content (videos, photos, Tweets, Wikimapia entries, flight logs) that can be interrogated using OSI techniques; (ii) Descriptive content — written/descriptive materials (media articles, NGO witness statements) that cannot be examined using OSI techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat examinable content as primary for verification; descriptive content should be summarised and used for context but is not the focus of OSI techniques. Some written items can be examinable depending on their form (e.g., photo of death certificate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue all reasonable lines of enquiry (including alternative explanations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to pursue all lines of reasonable enquiry including those leading towards evidence that may explain the attack or suggest alternative attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively pursue alternative possibilities and avenues of investigation to avoid confirmation bias. This includes investigating both immediate acts and surrounding events that could be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate algorithmic and access bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of algorithmic effects and counterbalance them: algorithms influence results based on device, location, prior history and other factors. Use advanced and varied search terms, multiple search engines and browsers and research accounts to reduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use varied search syntax, multiple engines and browsers. Create research accounts and deliberately shape their algorithmic profile. Delete cookies/browsing data where appropriate and record steps taken to mitigate algorithmic selection effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Mnemonic for preservation and tagging examinable content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any link you discover which you consider could amount to relevant information or evidence should be placed in the Mnemonic archiving sheet so Mnemonic can preserve the content. Tag examinable content to signpost the system to bring it into Uwazi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive every relevant link; Mnemonic will handle long-term preservation. Ensure content is entered into Mnemonic with appropriate tags/flags for Uwazi ingestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and cite the Original Online Source (earliest online source)
rubrics_metrics.description: For examinable content, always try to find the earliest online source (the Original Online Source) of the full text, video, or image. The earliest user should be cited as the source even if their post isn’t how you first discovered it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve and cite the original where possible. If a later version is higher-quality, preserve that too. If an earlier source is discovered after entry, update the report and note it in Research Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local preservation: maintain investigator copies and consistent filenames
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your own copies for reference in your private cloud folder; download pictures and videos relevant to your investigation and name them using the incident naming convention (incidentID_photox, incidentID_videox).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After uploading to the shared preservation system, delete local downloads when instructed; keep naming consistent and unique per media item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite imagery handling and captioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Satellite imagery is not considered at risk of removal and need not be preserved, but download for review as subscriptions may be time limited. Include a caption below satellite imagery with capture date and provider credit (e.g., (Courtesy of Google/DigitalGlobe)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct capture time/date. Group 'before and after' imagery in Uwazi and link to the event. For Google Earth Pro images, include provider as shown on screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification & Analysis procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification includes geolocation, chronolocation, corroboration and describing your content. This verification work must be clearly displayed within the Incident Assessment, with descriptive notes, cross-references and screenshots where helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification notes form a living document and must be cross-referenced via hyperlinks. Maintain accessible descriptions aimed at readers familiar with geolocation/chronolocation/cross-referencing. Detailed expert geolocation reports may be prepared later if required for specific proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Assessment as living neutral report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incident Assessment is the living document containing all verification work and conclusions; it should be a neutral description and technical analysis of the information uncovered. It is not a formal expert report; investigators may comment on any matters relevant to informing the reader about what happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Style Guide for language; present findings neutrally and comprehensively. Use the Incident Assessment Template sections (Introduction, Analysis of examinable content, Timeline, Questions, Statements, Conclusion, Further Action).

rubrics_metrics.name: No formal confidence gradings; use language of confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not attribute formal confidence gradings or degrees of likelihood to any findings or conclusions. Use language of confidence such as “appears to be”, “suggests”, “indicates”, or “strongly indicates/suggests.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-use of uncertainty language if there is a basis for certainty; use absolute statements only when justified (e.g., if item posted on 12 March, 'must have taken place on or before 12 March').

rubrics_metrics.name: Casualty reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are advised not to attempt to count casualties. We will authoritatively report civilian deaths only where direct examinable evidence exists (images of death certificates, hospital papers, tombstones) that can be matched with footage of bodies or patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include casualty estimate ranges from other sources as Descriptive Content but do not opine on their veracity unless you can analyse them using examinable evidence. Prefer neutral descriptions (avoid overuse of 'civilian' unless legally certain; use 'military personnel' if someone could be a fighter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic imagery handling and censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Only include graphic imagery in your report if the situation demands it. If you must include graphic imagery, censor any dead bodies, blood, and/or gore unless it is relevant to a point under discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pixelate images sufficiently that no discernible identity or extent of injuries remain. Use tools (e.g., SnagIt) and document censoring steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of neutral language and style guide conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Style Guide: use neutral language, standard date & time formats, decimal coordinates with hyperlinks, consistent reporting of casualties, conventions for images/satellite imagery/graphic imagery, footnotes and hyperlinking of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperlink sources in-text and footnote them for printed products. When an offline item is referenced, hyperlink it anyway for Mnemonic identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote and hyperlink practice
rubrics_metrics.description: All source references should appear as hyperlinks in the text of your report and should also be footnoted in case a report is delivered in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including information from a source, hyperlink directly to it. For offline or removed content, include the link to enable Mnemonic identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovering and updating earlier sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Your report should be comprehensive enough to allow a user to find the earliest instance of an item. If you discover an earlier version after entry, edit your report to add it and note this in Research Notes; try to enter the earliest complete version in Uwazi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss with team leader if an earlier version is discovered after Uwazi entry; annotate changes in Research Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uwazi data entry standards and field completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Populate Uwazi fields consistently: Incident Title, CIVHARM ID, Date (assessed/prima facie), Reported civilian deaths/injuries (as assessed), Description, Level of investigation (detailed or stub), Geolocation in decimal, Oblast, Type of object affected, Type of attack, Investigator Responsible, Red Flags, Content-level fields (title, original title, posted date/time, filmed date, description, geolocation, content_type, people visible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drop-downs and thesaurus where indicated. Populate 'site significance' only where appropriate. Attach Actor entries and link entities/incident groups properly. Use generated IDs and link archived links. Follow guidance for 'colocated', 'direct vicinity' or 'general area'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Assessment Template structure and required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Incident Assessment Template: include Incident ID, Location, Coordinates (hyperlink to Google Maps), Date (Prima Facie and Assessed), Time (Assessed in EET), Key Findings (2-4 bullets), Introduction with background summary/descriptive content and description of search process, Analysis of examinable content (including timeline and detailed description of events), Questions to address, Statements from parties to the conflict, Conclusion, and Further Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe searches used and their success. In Analysis, include date/time of social media posts and verification work, with hyperlinks and screenshots where useful. Note what you cannot explain and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging off and session security checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: When finishing an investigation session: save important links and leads in search log and links sheets; enter links into Mnemonic; upload content to Incident folder; turn off Hunchly and close all tabs and browsers; delete downloads and empty trash; power off laptop when at risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps ensure replicability and security between sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Team will communicate via Slack for general discussion and Signal group chat for particularly sensitive information. Do not use personal conversation threads or unrelated threads for investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss research progress, source evaluation and issues frequently and clearly. Use appropriate channel for sensitivity level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling restricted-content viewing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a platform requires proof of identity to view graphic content, it is permissible to transfer the link and watch it using another account that is sufficiently verified (such as regular Bellingcat account) provided that while outside J&A workstream you only watch the video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record actions and ensure no interactions are made; preserve link and provenance in logs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of background content for disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all relevant content and background content for disclosure purposes. Preserve all relevant material and be prepared to produce background information if required in legal processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure preservation actions (Mnemonic, Uwazi) and local records (Hunchly, Research Notes) document how content was located and handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal briefing and investigator role boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators will be provided with a legal briefing covering evidentiary principles and the substantive law applicable (e.g., IHL, war crimes, crimes against humanity). Investigators should document incidents to the highest standard but should not comment on the legality of an attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Legal Briefing to guide factual inquiries; discuss with legal team about relevance of evidence and lines of inquiry; investigators may comment on matters that inform the reader but should avoid legal conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of evidence and admissibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must gather evidence in accordance with rules on admissibility and weight; consider testing of evidence, fairness and exclusion issues, and pursue lines of enquiry that may affect admissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with legal team early; record searches and preservation steps so chain-of-custody/admissibility issues are documented. Retain background content to support disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red flag identification for SGBV and CAAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Review content for red flags related to sexual and gender-based violence (Annex III) and crimes against and affecting children (Annex IV); flag and handle such content per annex guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When red flags are present, document reason for flagging and follow special handling/privacy protocols in Annex II/III/IV. Only include graphic or identifying imagery when strictly necessary and follow censoring protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording device and research account metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Record device and research account information in the Device Log Sheet, including research account details so they can be traced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an auditable trail of which accounts were used, VPN nodes, device IDs and any deviations with memos and approvals recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hunchly noise reduction and profile hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need to do something unrelated to the factual enquiry, use a different browser to reduce amount of noise in Hunchly. Ensure you are logged out of other accounts and logged into passive research accounts where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contaminating Hunchly recordings with unrelated browsing; do personal tasks in separate browser/profile; delete accidental personal recordings via lead researcher if necessary.
